seoTitle: Free .htaccess to nginx Converter - Rewrite Rules
metaDescription: Translate common Apache .htaccess rules (Redirect, RewriteRule, ErrorDocument, Header, Expires) into nginx config. Unsupported lines are flagged. Free.
intro: Converts common Apache .htaccess directives to nginx syntax, including redirects, rewrite rules with conditions, error pages and headers, and marks anything it cannot translate as a TODO.
why: Switching a site from Apache to nginx means rewriting every .htaccess rule by hand, because nginx has no per-directory override files and uses a different rewrite model. Redirect chains, www and HTTPS rules and front-controller patterns are the parts that break most often. This tool handles the common cases and converts RewriteCond and RewriteRule pairs, flags such as R, L, NC, F and G, ErrorDocument, Options -Indexes, headers and expiry rules. It will not cover every Apache feature, so unsupported lines stay in the output as "# TODO" comments for you to resolve. It saves the typing but not the review: always check the result and run nginx -t before reloading.
howTo: Paste the contents of your .htaccess file into the input box.
Run the conversion and read the nginx directives it produces.
Resolve every "# TODO" line, put the rules in the right server or location block, and test with nginx -t.

faq.q: What is converted and what is not?
faq.a: Redirect, RedirectMatch, RewriteRule with RewriteCond (HTTPS, host, URI, query, filename checks), ErrorDocument, Options, DirectoryIndex, Header set, ExpiresByType and Require or Deny. Anything else becomes a TODO comment.

faq.q: Where do I put the output?
faq.a: Most lines belong in a server or location block. Expiry rules produce a map block that goes in the http context. The tool does not know your layout, so place them yourself.

faq.q: Can I trust the result without testing?
faq.a: No. Apache and nginx evaluate rewrites differently, and the converter is a pattern-based translation. Run nginx -t, then test real URLs for redirects and loops before going live.

faq.q: Why do some RewriteCond rules become TODO?
faq.a: Conditions on variables the tool does not map, or back-references that cannot be carried safely, are left for you. It is safer to flag them than to guess.
